li.label: made it right
li.description: I broke the window and I mended it, every bit, even the crooked corner I had to do twice.

li.label: said sorry in front of everyone
li.description: I had to stand up at supper and say sorry to everybody. My ears are still hot.

li.label: told off by the whole council
li.description: The whole council told me off, all of them at once, for one window. I keep out of the council's way now.

li.label: stories round the fire
li.description: Stories round the fire after the fighting, none of them about raiders. The children sat so close their faces went red.

li.label: shown the walls
li.description: I've seen the walls and the gate and where the watch stands. They're strong. I checked.

li.label: nobody came
li.description: I was frightened and they said I'd get over it. I'm still frightened. Now I'm frightened on my own.

li.label: looked after me
li.description: When everything was awful, they stayed with me through all of it. I sit next to them at every meal now.

li.label: said goodbye
li.description: We went out to the grave and I said goodbye properly, with a flower and a stone and the words I'd practiced.

li.label: too busy to be sad
li.description: They keep me so busy I don't have time to be sad. The sad is still there. It waits until bedtime.

li.label: left alone with it
li.description: They said time would help, so I go to bed early and lie there waiting for it to.

li.label: morning lessons
li.description: Lessons every morning now. I grumble, but I can spell better than some of the grown-ups.

li.label: learning by working
li.description: I followed the builders about all day, fetching and carrying and holding things steady. Tomorrow they're letting me use the hammer.

li.label: allowed to run free
li.description: No lessons, no chores. I spent the whole day up a tree and it was the best day.

li.label: we sorted it out
li.description: We fought over the den, and the grown-ups sorted it out. Now there are rules, and you have to knock.

li.label: allowed to see the world
li.description: The council said yes. Next time anyone goes out, I'm going with them. I've been packed for two days.

li.label: worried for my young one
li.description: My young one is going out with the next journey, and the council said yes. I'll worry until they're home again.

li.label: kept at home
li.description: Not this year, they said. They said that last year. I'll be old before they let me past the fields.

li.label: a taste of the road
li.description: We walked out past the fields, further than I've ever been, and came back at dusk. I want to go further next time.

li.label: one more look at the hills
li.description: I walked to the hills and sat at the top, looking back at everything we built. My legs will complain for a week.

li.label: walked to the hills with them
li.description: I walked them out to the hills and heard how this place began, back when there was nothing here but grass.

li.label: too far for old legs
li.description: I set out for the hills and my knees gave out halfway. I sat on a rock until they came looking, and was walked home like a child.

li.label: kept in like an invalid
li.description: I asked to see the hills once more and they said it was too far. I'm old, not made of paper.

li.label: fussed over
li.description: The council made me sit for the doctor like a child at bath time. Prodded, poked and handed a remedy, and not one of them asked what I wanted.

li.label: trusted with my own body
li.description: The council said I know my own body, and left it to me. The doctor keeps leaving remedies where I'll find them.

li.label: drove a hard bargain
li.description: I let the doctor look, and got a week off the worst chore for it. Best trade I've made in years.

li.label: heard the colony's story
li.description: The old one told us how this place began, the hard winters and the people who aren't here anymore. It went on long past bedtime, and I didn't want it to stop.

li.label: told the colony's story
li.description: I told them all of it, from the first day on, and they stayed to the end. Some of the young ones cried at the parts they'd never heard.

li.label: my story written down
li.description: Every name and every winter, written down in a proper book where it'll last. I keep finding things to add.

li.label: nobody wanted the story
li.description: I offered them the whole story of this place and they said another time. There won't be many other times.

li.label: a pupil at last
li.description: I have a pupil, a small, patient one who asks good questions and doesn't mind waiting while I find the word.

li.label: the old one's pupil
li.description: The old one is teaching me everything. Slowly, with a lot of sitting down. I like the sitting down.

li.label: pushed aside
li.description: Children belong with children, they said, as if the old belong on a shelf. The little one still comes to my chair in the evenings.

li.label: warm at last
li.description: A warm room at last, and a full night's sleep. My hands work properly in the mornings again.

li.label: gave up my warm room
li.description: I gave the old one my room by the stove. My new room is cold enough to see my breath in the mornings.

li.label: company by the fire
li.description: They sit with me by the fire in the evenings and keep it fed. Most nights I doze off before it burns down.

li.label: cold in the bones
li.description: No wood to spare for an old one, the council said. I sleep in my coat now.

li.label: the old way stands
li.description: The council backed the way I've always done it. Thirty years count for something.

li.label: a chance to try my way
li.description: The council's letting me try it my way for a season. Now I just have to be right.

li.label: overruled
li.description: The council took the other side. I'll do it their way. I'll do it with my mouth shut, mostly.

li.label: worked it out together
li.description: We argued for a day and worked side by side for another, and came out with a way that's half of each.

li.label: someone's keeping watch
li.description: There's a watch on the walls at night now. I slept through till morning for the first time in a week.

li.label: standing the night watch
li.description: Half the night on the walls, watching an empty field so a worrier can sleep. I'm the one yawning now.

li.label: talked me down
li.description: They went through every one of my worries with me, and what we'd do about each. Some of them look silly now. Not all.

li.label: my worries waved away
li.description: The council said the walls are fine. They would. They sleep at night.

li.label: keeper of the record
li.description: I'm the colony's record keeper, by the council's word, and the notebook has a shelf of its own now.

li.label: my notes kept private
li.description: I can keep my record, as long as nobody has to read it. That's not what a record is for.

li.label: the kind pages read out
li.description: They read out the kind things from the colony's record at supper. There were more than I'd have guessed, and one of them was about me.

li.label: the snow day
li.description: A whole day out in the snow, sliding on the slope until dark. My hands were frozen stiff and I didn't care.

li.label: the children's race
li.description: The children's race, round the string course by the fields, with cheering all the way. Who won is still being argued about.

li.label: the gleanings shared
li.description: The children came back from the stubble with full baskets and told us, very seriously, who had found what.

li.label: the children's trees
li.description: A tree planted this spring, with a stone beside it to say whose it is. One day there'll be shade there.
